1) the performance criteria (PCs) for the QIs in the pre-analytic phase are achievable, 2) the performance targets are realistic and 3) the PCs and targets for the QIs are harmonized and can be used as reference standards for the evaluation of quality of pre-analytic activities.

the QIs are the most appropriate and useful tool to assess the quality of the pre-analysis phase and that the performance targets for each QI should be established in agreement with a classification based on the state-of-the art of laboratory performance.
QI-based performance specifications are achievable, desirable and minimum performance criteria for the pre-ananalytical phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification, implementation and monitoring in the clinical laboratory of QIs and performance criteria for the pre-analysis phase, with the aim to support laboratories and healthcare institutions in improving the quality and efficiency of the TTP.

the definition of a list of performance criteria and quality indicators to be used for monitoring the pre-analytic phase, and with the definition of achievable performance targets based on data collected by several laboratories worldwide.
the development of QIs for the TTP, with the identification of the performance criteria, and with the establishment of achievable and realistic target values for each QI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the definition of QIs for the TTP, and particularly for the pre-ananalytical phase, represents a valuable tool for the assessment of laboratory performance and for the improvement of laboratory quality.

the pre-analytic phase is a key element for the overall quality of laboratory results, that it should be included within the quality system of every laboratory and that it should be monitored by means of a set of QIs, which are currently available and have been validated by a wide consensus of international experts.
the performance criteria for QIs are achievable, and that the implementation of the QI program is an important step in the process of quality improvement in the pre-analytic phase of the TTP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the performance criteria and the quality indicators represent a valuable tool for monitoring the quality of the TTP, and that the definition of achievable performance targets based on these QIs is a key step in the quality improvement projects.
the identification of achievable performance criteria for the pre-ananalytical phase represents a promising approach to the improvement of the overall quality of laboratory services.
the definition of performance criteria is a useful and necessary tool for the improvement of quality in the TTP.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to the already known analytical quality specifications, the establishment of achievable performance targets for the pre-ananalytical phase is a necessary step towards a complete quality assurance system.
QIs and performance criteria for the pre-analystical phase are now available to be used by the clinical laboratory community for the improvement of quality in the TTP.

, by adopting the proposed approach, the pre-analytic phase can be considered as a whole, with the aim of identifying and implementing the most suitable quality indicators, thus allowing the monitoring of the overall performance and the identification of critical steps in the TTP.
